folga-do-host.d: Memory left for the operating system after vLLM and after what the process and the driver hold beyond the GMU budget (~12.4 GiB on an idle Qwen node). The OS, the page cache and the load eat into it. Estimated with the node idle: below ~8 GiB, the load drove MemAvailable close to zero in the recipes, the zone where the GB10 may hard reset.

fator-do-alocador.d: Ratio between what vLLM's hybrid allocator charges per context token and the physical bytes: the page or group padding that grows with the context. GLM and Qwen ≈ 1 (their excess is fixed per request); DeepSeek ≈ 2.04 and MiMo ≈ 1.15 are per-token readings, because their published boots use a single max-model-len.

custo-fixo-por-requisicao.d: The part of the KV that a request occupies whatever its context: the physical state (linear attention, SWA windows) plus the block IDs the hybrid allocator charges for each state group, each ID costing one page across all the layers of the group. GLM: ≈ 1.58 GiB with compact drafter pages, ≈ 7.6 GiB without them. Qwen: ≈ 0.47 GiB (FP32 state) or ≈ 0.09 GiB (BF16).

estimativa-de-graphs.d: With VLLM_MEMORY_PROFILER_ESTIMATE_CUDAGRAPHS=1 (the default), vLLM records a test capture and subtracts the estimated graph memory from the KV pool. On GLM the estimate was 2.43 GiB and the real usage −0.19 GiB (~2.6 GiB of KV reserved and never used). With 0 (DeepSeek), the pool loses nothing and the graphs come out of the host headroom.

modelo-de-custo.d: Estimate of the time of one decode step: bytes read (experts, dense, drafter, KV and state) ÷ effective bandwidth + collective latency. Dividing the tokens per step by that time gives the tok/s ceiling.

experts-distintos.d: Expected number of different experts touched in a layer when the step processes T tokens with top-k: \( \bar E = E[1-(1-1/E)^{k T}] \). It grows with the batch and with speculation, which is why it makes the step more expensive in MoE.

alfa-equivalente.d: Constant conditional acceptance that, in the geometric model, reproduces the same τ as a measured acceptance curve with the same k. It lets you use the simple formula without losing the measured number.

capture-sizes.d: Batch sizes (in tokens) for which vLLM records CUDA graphs. With speculation, they must be multiples of k+1 up to max_num_seqs × (k+1); a batch between two sizes is padded up to the next one; only a batch larger than the last captured size runs eager, which is slower.

padding-de-cabecas.d: Adding fake heads (with zeroed output) so that the total divides by TP. For example: GLM 64 → 66 on TP3 (96 made the logits collapse); DeepSeek 64 → 72 with groups 8 → 9 and sink −∞.
